title: Spencer knitting at Fifi's Monte Carlo, his death, and Specs Powell
summary: At Fifi's Monte Carlo, Spencer knitted an afghan on his doctor's advice; he died in 1944 while Procope was in the army, and Specs Powell had filled in for him.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: What was it, bronchitis or tuberculosis, or something?

I really don't know. Because I tell you what, he had been under the doctor's care. Because we were playing in this little club, Fifi's Monte Carlo, on the East Side. That was a tremendous club, you know.

What street? About 54th Street, on the East Side, someplace. It was a tremendous club. It was a great big beautiful room and they had a band in there. So Fifi, the fellow's name was Fifi somebody they called him. He was one of them socialites, you know, with all the Vanderbilts and the Astors and the whatchacallit used to go. Cholly Knickerbocker, that sort of thing. So he bought out the store next door and turned it into a little small nightclub for the people who were waiting, to give them someplace to wait till they could get in the big room, and hired John Kirby's

band to play for the people who were waiting. And the decor was beautiful. It was like palm trees and all this, and he bought us suits, uniforms, green, beautiful, you know, white jackets. Oh, it was beautiful, real beautiful, yeah. So while we were playing there we had a nice room upstairs, you know. We could lounge around between sets. And Spencer had been to the doctor and the doctor gave -- told him to knit. Knit, you know. Knit, for therapy, I suppose. And he knitted an afghan. Oh, it must have been a huge thing, you know, you could use for a bedspread or something. And he just sat there knitting it. And the people, the people who had known Spencer before, they'd come up and look at him and say, 'I don't believe it.' You know, because Spencer was such a rowdy sort of a person. I'll use that word, you know. He was into everything, hollering and running, you know. Then all of a sudden he's sitting there like -- that was his -- that's where he ended up.

I remember he lived over in Brooklyn, and we took him home to Brooklyn. Then I was in the Army. I was in Camp Breckenridge, down in Kentucky. And my wife wrote me a letter and she said Spencer had died.
Now, who came in and replaced Spencer?
Let's see, now. What is that man's name? Specs Powell. Specs Powell. A very good drummer.
A very, very good drummer. Yeah.
Uptown. Uptown. And Specs had filled in for him then. Then Spencer came back. You know, that's how we knew that Specs was a pretty good drummer. Yeah. Uh-huh.
